context: A boss mentors a uni intern
purpose: Teach: 被疑/面会/先送り/白紙/水質/非公式/たたき台/商事

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 蓮、被疑となる前の対応、企業の運命を左右する。
lines.en: Ren — how you handle things before suspicion arises determines the company's fate.
lines.style: Measured, direct. Sets the weight of the moment without drama. Slight pause after the name—making this personal, not abstract. Steady eye contact.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 弁護士との面会、若手も同席することがあるんですね。
lines.en: So juniors do get to sit in on counsel meetings?
lines.style: Curious but respectful. Slightly careful phrasing—testing whether this is a privilege or routine. Open, genuinely interested. Not performing eagerness.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 判断、先送りせず、即決を心がけろ。
lines.en: Make your decisions now. Don't defer them.
lines.style: Firm, economical. Each phrase lands separately. No softening—this is instruction, not suggestion. Brief, because the point is clear.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。白紙のページ、自分で埋める覚悟、必要ですね。
lines.en: Yes. I understand — I need to be ready to fill in the blanks myself.
lines.style: Quiet acknowledgment. Slight underbreath on the opening. Processing the weight of what was just said, not just agreeing. Sincere, a little self-aware about the commitment.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 水質や環境調査、外部委託も活用しろ。
lines.en: Outsource the water-quality and environmental surveys too.
lines.style: Practical addendum. Same measured pace as before—not hurried, not emphatic. The voice of someone used to delegating wisely.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 非公式な交流、人脈作りに、役立つんですね。
lines.en: Unofficial connections like that—they really do help build a network?
lines.style: Tentative question, framed carefully. Seeking confirmation more than information. Slightly deferential—asking permission to trust his own instinct about people.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: たたき台、毎日、自分で書いてみろ。
lines.en: Write a draft yourself every day.
lines.style: Direct instruction, no ceremony. The voice of someone who expects this will be done. Not harsh—just matter-of-fact, the way a mentor speaks when respect is already there.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 商事系の業務、勉強したいです。
lines.en: I'd like to develop expertise in trading-firm work.
lines.style: Sincere statement of intention, understated. Not performed enthusiasm. Quiet, a little tentative—putting forward what matters without overselling it.
